note: Same prospect and same assessment as the discovery leg, with occupation now confirmed on this call — "I'm a financial advisor" — alongside owning a company with many employees, which satisfies the successful criterion outright. Health is the neglected area of an otherwise well-run life. He misses on the three criteria describing starting point and ability to pay now. Income fails on liquidity, not earnings: "we're in the middle of a home remodel. It's costing $600,000. And that pretty much drains us of all of our liquid money", set against "I make a decent living and so I can find a way to make that happen" — capacity without cash, which the ICP observations already identify as the pattern income screening wrongly filters out. good_to_great fails because his own framing is recovery from injury and decline, not refinement. not_deconditioned fails on 215 lb at 6'1" with self-reported 28-30% body fat, no training routine and an aversion to gyms. Judged strictly on the five criteria as written this is close to outside; I have called it edge because two of the three misses restate the same underlying fact about his starting condition, and the income miss is about timing rather than means. The criterion that should have governed this call does not exist in the stated ICP at all — nothing in it asks whether a prospect with ruptured cervical discs and an elbow that will not extend should be sold loaded overhead kettlebell work.
